Access controls in a network design

Unit 1 · Week 13 · Lesson 3 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Open the network-design chapter and its learning resources. Use paper or a local editor as appropriate, with fictional data and disposable practice copies. The suggested 55-minute lesson is flexible.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

1. Access controls in a network design

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Explain the goal and the expected independent outcome. Match controls to unauthorised-access risks. This is ungraded textbook learning. Suggested times can be adjusted to the class. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-design. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

2. Retrieval and explanation

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual retrieval, then partner comparison

Read access does not imply write permission. A firewall applies configured traffic rules, while application/file permissions control other operations. Allow silent thinking before discussion. Ask a learner to justify an answer before revealing the explanation. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-design. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

3. Threat and control links

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked table and teacher explanation

Introduce least privilege as giving only required access. Distinguish permitted connectivity from permission to edit a resource. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-design. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

4. A shared administrator login

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Predict, model and explain

Separate limited accounts reduce unnecessary power and improve activity attribution. Logs still need integrity and context. Pause for predictions before discussing the expected result. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-design. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

5. A rule with a purpose

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Guided paired practice

A web connection rule does not grant export or file-edit permission. Ask learners where each decision is enforced. Swap explaining and checking roles so both learners articulate the reasoning. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-design. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

6. Independent practice

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent application with optional support

Use paper predictions. Keep legitimate student reading available while protecting staff changes. No live rule deployment. Offer the relevant worked example if needed, then use a changed case to check independent understanding. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-design. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

7. A choice to explain

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Whole-class response and justification

B. Separation structures communication but its configured forwarding and permissions determine access. Give thinking time and collect reasons, without recording scores. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-design. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

8. Exit explanation

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual reflection and fresh explanation

Require a particular role, operation and resource, not merely the word security. Use the response to select the next explanation or practice activity. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-design.
